before: Concurrent edits that wrote one paragraph or run property twice, or edited a joined paragraph, ended sessions; some concurrent split and join edits left replicas, cold joiners, and exports with different text. A remote update the replica could not materialize ended the session, a local caret kept its offset while peers edited before it, and `create` wrote no seed record.
after: Each replica shows the first live copy of a duplicated singleton, adopted children are listed where they are shown before a structural edit, and derived parent indexes agree between live and cold replicas. A replica that cannot materialize a remote update pauses edits and heals on the next clean update, the local caret follows remote edits, and `create` records its seed so a second merged seed reports `concurrent-seed`. A split-text alias whose rewrite is still in flight keeps its last read value instead of reading as plain text. A survivor shows joined paragraphs in the order their joins were written, the same on every replica. A split-text range whose live anchors crossed reads as an empty slice instead of refusing the document, and a refused local edit realigns from a full rebuild. A replica rebuilds every ancestor a changed node was shown under so split losers a peer detached leave the view; remote cursors follow text typed before them until the peer publishes again. Enter inside a run records the head and tail as aliases of the run's text even when the tail moves to a new paragraph, so a peer's concurrent typing in that run survives; an unmounted editor withdraws its caret from presence. Undo restores the selection the undone change was made from. A replica decides again which parent shows a child that several parents list after every structural change, and rebuilds both parents when the answer moves; a child a removed join survivor had taken over shows under its other parent. Live replicas then match a cold read of the same shared state. Undo carries the restored selection across text peers changed since the step. A failing WebRTC peer link keeps the room ready and reports itself as the status reason. A refused edit that waits on a peer's update stops counting as transient after 20 in a row. Each published selection endpoint carries an optional digest of the paragraph text it counts in, and a receiver holds a peer's offset until its own text matches. A removed alias field reads as an overwrite in flight only while a pending update holds that field's successor. A join survivor adopts again a child that is restored, or whose record arrives, after the join, and a paragraph that arrives already joined hands its children over at once. Two peers pasting several paragraphs at one position both stay ready: a rebuilt paragraph keeps its unchanged children in place in the shared list. The local caret and the carets peers show stay next to the same character when one remote update changes text on both sides of them, and text a peer inserts exactly at a caret goes after it. Lifecycle edits, such as a first footnote, mint ids striped by their author, and new header, footer, and media parts take part numbers from their author's stripe. Paragraph ids that new table cells mint are scoped to their author, so a caret never names two paragraphs. The local caret is anchored on the shared character beside it before each remote update, and after the update stands beside that character wherever it shows, including a copy that a split or join moved; the editor maps by text only when the session carries no answer. Each published selection endpoint carries an optional shared character, and a receiver that shows it places the peer's caret beside it. Text that replaces a word keeps none of the replaced word's letters that are no longer than the change on both sides, so a peer's concurrent deletion of the old word leaves the new word whole. An edit inside a content control's properties, such as clearing its placeholder flag, is written to the paragraph text that holds the control. The operation gate refuses, before it commits, an edit of a paragraph whose text a held-back update carries, and the status snapshot says when edits wait; the status snapshot counts failures and marks an error the session heals by itself. A peer's published caret whose paragraph a join removed stands beside its character in the paragraph that shows it. Undo of typing that a peer's split or join moved removes the moved copies, by recording the typed characters as deleted, and redo withdraws that record; an undo no longer skips such a step and undoes an older one. Collaboration hooks key their room owner by hook instance, so roots that hydrate the same tree and Vue composables called outside a component keep a room each. A wrapper's fixed parts, such as a content control's properties with many list choices, travel whole in the shared text up to 32,768 nodes, and a value beyond that refuses the seed or the edit with `too-many-nodes` instead of losing the control. Undo of moved typing covers every character of the step. Compaction measures the gain against a fresh build of the current content.
reason: No stored field or update meaning changes. Released participants refused the duplicated-singleton states that now resolve, so no conflict gets a different survivor. Adoption is written with ordinary child-array splices that released readers already interpret. The remaining changes are replica-local caching and index derivation. The seed record uses the existing `docx-collaboration-seeds-v1` array that released `create-or-join` replicas already write and watch. Healing and caret mapping are replica-local. Join order is derived from existing `replacedBy` writes; a released replica still orders by arrival, which it already did inconsistently, so mixed rooms gain no new disagreement. Reading a crossed range as empty changes only how a replica renders state released replicas refused outright. Remote cursor mapping uses the existing presence payload and is replica-local. Cross-paragraph split aliases use the existing `splitTextSource` field that released readers already resolve. Keeping unchanged children in place writes fewer ordinary child-array splices that released readers already interpret. Contest decisions and adoption release are derived indexes and caching on each replica; the shared state and the first-in-document-order rule are unchanged, so a released replica that rebuilds from shared state reaches the same document. Selection mapping, link reporting and the refusal count are replica-local. The presence digest is an optional field: released readers build addresses from paragraphId and offset only and ignore it, and a payload without it resolves as before. The published character is an optional presence field: released readers ignore it, a malformed one is dropped, and a receiver that does not show the character uses the offset as before. Anchoring the local caret is replica-local and writes nothing to shared state. Which letters a local edit keeps, and where a content control property edit is written, are decided by the editing replica before it writes ordinary text operations that released readers already apply. The gate, the status counters, and resolving a published character without its paragraph are replica-local and write nothing to shared state. The undo writes ordinary deletion records in the existing `docx-text-deletions-v1` map, which every replica of this format already reads, and the redo deletes the records it wrote. Room ownership in the hooks is replica-local. The larger bound only admits values the encoder writes; a reader still drops a value beyond it. Compaction reads the stored state on the server and writes the same new-generation format as before.
